privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.html:
The free CLI

Your source code and the evidence aletheore scan produces stay on your machine. Evidence is written to .aletheore/ in the repository you scanned, and your source code is never uploaded. The CLI reports no usage data.

The CLI does contact a few services on its own. By default a scan looks up public advisory and license data for your dependencies, which sends dependency names and versions (not your code) to OSV.dev and to the package registries; --no-check-vulnerabilities and --no-check-licenses turn those lookups off. It also checks PyPI for a newer release; ALETHEORE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 turns that off.

If the CLI itself crashes, it sends a crash report to our error-tracking provider, Sentry: the exception details and stack trace, the Aletheore, operating system and Python versions, and recent log lines, with your home directory replaced by ~ and command-line arguments, the machine name and local variables removed. An exception message can still name a file or path from the project you were scanning. Nothing is sent unless the CLI crashes. Crash reporting is on by default; aletheore config crash-reporting off (or ALETHEORE_CRASH_REPORTING=0) turns it off.

If you use an AI-assisted audit command, evidence, not source code, is sent to whichever LLM provider you configure, using your own API key.

The GitHub App (Aletheore Flash and AIR)

Installing the GitHub App is a different trust boundary, and source code does reach our servers.

We clone your repository to run a scan. For repositories we scan repeatedly, a working copy is kept on our scan worker between scans rather than deleted after each one - this is what lets a later scan process only what changed instead of starting from nothing every time. That copy is deleted when you uninstall the app, remove the repository from the app's access, or request deletion, and is not retained after any of them.

What is stored long-term is derived evidence: secrets findings, dependency graphs, endpoint health rows, and generated documentation.

What we send to our LLM provider depends on the feature, and three of them are not evidence:

  • Flash review (automated pull request review) sends the pull request's diff - that is your source code, for the changed lines - along with limited surrounding file context. For paid installations, that diff is also kept for up to 30 days in a short-lived cache, so a near-identical diff doesn't get re-reviewed from scratch; it is deleted automatically once that window passes, or immediately on uninstall. Free-tier reviews are never cached - nothing about them is retained beyond the request itself.
  • AIRview Docs (generated API documentation) sends the source of individual public functions and classes - that is your source code - to write a short description of each one.
  • Managed audits and the rest of AIRview (the wiki and the dependency graph) send derived evidence, not source code.
  • Endpoint health fix suggestions send a short snippet of the surrounding code (about 30 lines) for a failing endpoint, along with its method, path, and status - that is your source code, to suggest a fix.

For paid (Flash and AIR) installations, our provider for Flash review is IndieRouter (GLM-5.3-Flash), which does not retain prompts or use them to train models, per IndieRouter's own published policy. If IndieRouter is unavailable, Flash review falls back to OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Luna), then DeepSeek.

Managed audits, the AIRview wiki, and AIRview Docs are written by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash via IndieRouter, which does not retain prompts or use them to train models, per IndieRouter's own published policy. If IndieRouter is unavailable, managed audits and the wiki fall back to DeepSeek directly, and Docs falls back to OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Luna), or to DeepSeek if OpenAI is also unavailable.

Endpoint health fix suggestions are written by GLM-5.3-Flash via IndieRouter, under the same no-retention policy. If IndieRouter is unavailable, this falls back to OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Luna), or to DeepSeek if OpenAI is also unavailable.

Free (Community plan) Flash review does not use IndieRouter. It runs through a different set of providers, tried in order until one succeeds: Groq, Google (Gemini), OpenAI's free-tier allowance, then OpenRouter.

What we store

For paid installations: your GitHub account or organization identity, the email address on your GitHub account, evidence snapshots from scans, findings you have dismissed, an audit log of administrative actions taken on your installation, signed audit reports, and, if configured, a Slack/Teams webhook URL and health-check monitoring settings.

Health-check results are private to your dashboard unless you explicitly turn on the public status API for your installation, which is off by default.

We do not sell this data or share it beyond the service providers necessary to run Aletheore: our LLM provider for the features listed above, our payment provider for billing, our email provider for transactional mail, and our error-tracking provider, which receives technical error reports from our servers (stack traces and error messages, with request data and local variables removed; a message can still name a repository or installation).

Deleting your data

Uninstalling the GitHub App erases everything held for that installation, including the retained working copy of your repository. The same erasure is available on demand from your dashboard without uninstalling. Both paths remove account-level records - your captured email address and any active sessions - once you have no other installation remaining.

Removing a single repository from the app's access deletes our retained working copy of it. The evidence and findings already derived from that repository are hidden from your dashboard and kept until you uninstall the app or request deletion.

Database backups are taken daily and the 14 most recent are kept, so erased data can remain in a backup for up to about two weeks before it is overwritten. We also keep a permanent record that a deletion took place - the installation ID, the account name, who requested it, and counts of what was removed - and nothing else.

Contact

Questions about this policy or a data deletion request: support@aletheore.com

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.html:
What Aletheore is

Aletheore is a repository audit tool: a local-first CLI, free for personal, noncommercial use under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, and paid GitHub App tiers for automated PR reviews, managed audits, Slack/Teams alerts, branch-protection Check Runs, and endpoint health monitoring. Using the CLI for or within a company or other organization is a commercial use and requires a separate commercial license, regardless of whether you also subscribe to a paid GitHub App tier.

The paid subscriptions

Two paid plans: Aletheore Flash ($10/month, monthly billing only) and Aletheore AIR ($29.99/month or $299.90/year, up to 3 team members, with additional members beyond the plan's included seats billed at $6.99/month each). See Pricing for full plan details. Subscriptions are billed and processed by our payment provider, Paddle, acting as merchant of record. By subscribing, you agree to Paddle's own terms of service in addition to these.

AI credit top-ups

Paid subscribers can buy extra AI credit at any time from the dashboard. Credit costs $1.15 per $1.00 of credit: the extra $0.15 is a service charge that covers payment processing. Tax is added at checkout where it applies. Purchased credit does not expire. Credit that has already been used cannot be returned, and refunds follow our Refund Policy.

Acceptable use

You may not use Aletheore to scan repositories you do not have the right to scan, or to circumvent security measures of systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

No warranty

Aletheore is provided as-is. The deterministic scanner is unit-tested and evidence-grounded, but no software is guaranteed to catch every issue in every repository.

Contact

Questions about these terms: support@aletheore.com

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.html:
How refunds work

Aletheore is sold through Paddle, which is the merchant of record for every purchase. We do not issue refunds ourselves: refund requests are handled by Paddle under Paddle's Refund Policy, together with any refund or withdrawal rights the law gives you where you live.

Under that policy you can ask Paddle for a refund within 14 days of a transaction. Paddle decides each request, and approval is not guaranteed. Your statutory rights, such as the right to withdraw from some digital contracts in the EU, EEA and UK, are not affected.

Cancelling

You can cancel at any time. A cancelled subscription stays active until the end of the billing period you have already paid for, and then does not renew. We do not offer prorated refunds for partial periods.

Credit top-ups

AI credit top-ups are one-off purchases and are covered by the same Paddle policy. Credit that has already been used cannot be returned.

How to request one

Use the link in your Paddle receipt email, or go to paddle.net and choose "Request refund". Questions about a charge can also go to support@aletheore.com.

security.title: Security
security.html:
Aletheore audits other people's code, so we hold ourselves to the same evidence-grounded standard we ask of you. This page describes what we actually do, not what a template says a security page should claim. Where we fall short of something you'd expect, we say so directly rather than leave it unstated.

Your source code

When the GitHub App runs a scan, your repository is cloned into a scan worker and analyzed. For a repository we scan only once, that clone is discarded afterward. For one we scan repeatedly, a working copy is kept on the scan worker between scans so a later scan can process only what changed - it is deleted on uninstall or a data-deletion request, and never otherwise retained. Only derived evidence, findings like secrets matches, dependency graphs, and endpoint health rows, is written to our database. What reaches our LLM provider depends on the feature: Flash review (automated PR review, Flash tier and up) sends the pull request's diff itself - your actual source code, for the changed lines - while managed audits and AIRview (AIR) send only derived evidence, never raw source files. See our Privacy Policy for the full data-handling breakdown.

GitHub App permissions

The GitHub App requests these permissions: repository contents (read and write), checks (write), pull requests (write), issues (read), repository metadata (read), and read access to the email address of the GitHub account that signs in. It subscribes to the check run, issue comment, pull request and push events. Pull request and checks write access are used to post reviews, comments and check runs. Contents write access exists for one optional feature: when you turn on Docs sync, Aletheore pushes the generated docs to a dedicated aletheore/docs-update branch and opens a pull request from it. It never pushes to your default branch, and an installation that has not turned Docs sync on never uses that access. The App does not request organization-wide admin permissions, and it cannot see or modify repository settings, other installed apps, or billing on your GitHub account.

Authentication and webhooks

Dashboard sign-in uses GitHub OAuth; we never see or store a GitHub password. Both inbound webhook sources we depend on, GitHub and Paddle, are verified against an HMAC signature before we act on the payload, and unsigned or mismatched deliveries are rejected outright. Authentication endpoints are rate-limited per source IP to slow credential-stuffing and session-fixation attempts.

Infrastructure

Traffic to the app is served over TLS. Application data lives in a Postgres database that is not exposed to the public internet; it's only reachable from our own backend services. Payment details are never handled by our servers, checkout and card data are processed entirely by our payment provider, Paddle, which is itself a Merchant of Record and PCI-DSS compliant. We do not see or store card numbers.

What we scan for, in ourselves

Every pull request and every push to master runs through the same class of checks we sell: container image scanning with Trivy, which blocks a merge outright on a HIGH or CRITICAL vulnerability with a known fix, CodeQL static analysis, and an SPDX software bill of materials generated for every service image. We also dogfood our own product: the Proof page shows Aletheore's own repo scanned by Aletheore's own CLI, and our status page is our own endpoint-health monitoring feature, pointed at ourselves.

Where we're honest about gaps

Aletheore is a small, early-stage team. We do not currently hold a SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar third-party compliance certification, and we don't claim to. If that's a hard requirement for your organization, tell us, it's useful signal for what to prioritize next.

Reporting a vulnerability

If you find a security issue in Aletheore, the app, the CLI, or this site, email support@aletheore.com with "security" in the subject line. We'll acknowledge reports and won't take legal action against good-faith, non-destructive testing aimed at reporting a vulnerability to us.
